tables.table: gla-decs-phase-1.zip/Phase 1/Phase 1_DE potential_v041011.xls#4.1 GIS output and carried data
header_rows: Data (namely the heat density of an MSOA) from tab 5.2 was entered into GIS software. The software grouped MSOAs according to their heat density and their adjacency. E.g. a 50kWh/m2 agglomeration consists of a group of neighbouring MSOAs that all have a heat density greater than 50kWh/m2. For each heat density their are several (1-20+) agglomerations, these are labelled XY where X= heat threshold and Y= agglomeration number. E.g. agglomeration 5007 is the seventh agglomeration for a heat density of 50kWh/m2.

Key to this work is the concept of threshold heat densities, agglomerations and MSOAs.
           *MSOA: is a census area of houses and businesses. It is  the basic area used for the input statistics on gas consumption, meters etc.
           *Agglomeration: this is a group of adjacent MSOAs with a heat density above a certain threshold.
           *Heat density threshold: this is a group of agglomerations all consisting of MSOAs above a given heat density.
